mode: read-only audit; no source, configuration, database, model, Q-table or evidence was modified
verdict: READY FOR FINAL DEMONSTRATION AND INTERVIEW WITH QUALIFIED CLAIMS; NOT PRODUCTION-READY

findings.type: confirmed defect (latent: reachable only if windows_srv is ever served)
findings.title: A windows_srv session still reaches the V1 Q-table as the PREVIOUS state of the next Linux session
files: ai-engine/rl_engine/deception_scorer.py: SessionScorer.process_session (Rank 7 gate tests only `active in UNSUPPORTED_PROFILES`; `state` = previousProfile is accepted because windows_srv is in PROFILES)
findings.evidence: Probe on a temporary copy of the shipped seed: session {deceptionProfile: ubuntu_22, previousProfile: windows_srv} -> learned=true, Q[windows_srv][ubuntu_22] 48.651 -> 56.4864. Production tables untouched.
findings.impact: docs/PERSONAS.md claims windows sessions are 'never learned'; true for the session itself, not for the transition out of it. Not reachable today (switch_profile.py refuses windows_srv; the Cowrie hook is off and not installed).
findings.remediation: In process_session, treat a previousProfile in UNSUPPORTED_PROFILES as no state (fall back to last servable) or skip learning; add a test.

findings.title: Rank 6 left backend/tests/deceptionProfile.test.js failing (2 tests) and its report did not run that suite
findings.evidence: Found and corrected during Rank 7 (assertions updated to the Rank 6 shadow record shape). Passes in this audit (part of 802/802).
findings.remediation: None outstanding; record that Rank 6 test claims were incomplete.

findings.title: cmd /c "a & b" (quoted form, the common attacker idiom) is answered as one unknown command
files: honeypot/windows_persona/shell.py: c_cmd (joins args with quotes kept: `" ".join(args[1:])`)
findings.evidence: WindowsShell().execute('cmd /c "whoami & hostname"') -> "'whoami & hostname' is not recognized..."
findings.remediation: Strip the outer quotes of the /c argument as cmd.exe does; add a test. Inert either way (no security impact).

findings.title: `cmd /c set X=Y` leaks the variable into the parent session
files: honeypot/windows_persona/shell.py: c_cmd (inner.__dict__.update(sh.__dict__) shares the env dict)
findings.evidence: Probe P3: AUDITVAR present in parent env after `cmd /c set AUDITVAR=1`.
findings.remediation: Give the child a copy of env.

findings.title: REVERSE_SHELL intent matches `-e` followed by 16+ alphanumerics (e.g. `echo -e aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`) in windows sessions; the collector then raises a CRITICAL 'High-Value: REVERSE_SHELL' alert
findings.remediation: Require powershell context and `-e(nc|ncodedcommand)` (make the suffix mandatory); add a negative corpus entry.

findings.title: Windows ATT&CK rules in mitreMapping.js are global, not persona-gated; path/keyword rules can apply to Linux sessions
files: backend/utils/windowsPersona.js: WINDOWS_COMMAND_TECHNIQUES (web.config, unattend.xml, \config\sam, reg save, powershell, cmd /c, iex)
findings.evidence: Test proves only the 17-command Linux corpus is unaffected. docs/PERSONAS.md says 'No Linux command matches them' and the code comment says Linux sessions 'map exactly as before' - overstated (e.g. `cat web.config` on Linux now maps to T1552.001).
findings.remediation: Either gate by persona like intent, or reword the claim to 'Windows-specific names and paths'.

findings.title: Per-line event amplification is bounded but not capped explicitly
findings.evidence: Probe P2: 62 events from one 7 KB line of 31 `cmd /c` segments; 100 events from nested -enc. Each unrecognised inner event emits cowrie.command.failed, which the parser forwards to the backend.
findings.remediation: Cap events per input line (e.g. 64) in WindowsShell.execute.

findings.title: Per-session virtual filesystem can hold ~16 MB (256 x 64 KB); no limit across concurrent sessions
findings.remediation: Add a total-bytes cap per session.

findings.title: One extra MongoDB read per UNKNOWN command at ingest
findings.remediation: Acceptable; optionally cache the served persona per session.

findings.title: Engine public /predict and /predict/honeypot callbacks (_notify) post predictions without captureSource; the backend route stores them as inputSource network_traffic (even honeypot ones)
findings.evidence: The backend's own pipeline uses /predict/internal and /predict/honeypot/internal, which never call _notify, so Demo A/B and PCAP replay are unaffected. Records from direct public calls show captureSource 'unknown'.
findings.remediation: Pass inputSource/captureSource through the callback or drop the callback for honeypot predictions.

findings.title: The structured sentinel.windows.command event is not consumed by the parser
findings.evidence: Category/ATT&CK ids from the simulator exist only in Cowrie's JSON log; the backend recomputes intent and ATT&CK from the command text.
findings.remediation: Document precisely, or add a handler.

findings.title: docs/COWRIE_COMPLETE_GUIDE.md:394 says switch_profile refuses windows_srv 'without --allow-unservable'; the flag no longer bypasses the refusal
Stale persona statements after Rank 7
files: README.md:45 ('the Windows persona is unsupported because Cowrie emulates only a Linux shell' - still true for production, but omits the experimental simulation)
docs/PERSONAS.md Rank 7 section: 'cmd /c|/k' (see F3), 'never learned' (see F1), 'No Linux command matches them' (see R1)

findings.title: Ranks 1 and 2 have no machine-readable evidence run under audit/; their evidence is test suites + docs. Ranks 3/4 evidence lives in ai-engine/experiments/ (qlearning_evidence_v2_20261113, session_ml_data_audit_20261113).
Readiness evidence has no expiry age; gate 10 is hard-coded NOT_MET so READY is unreachable by design (documented)

Not live-tested or not independently verifiable: live capture, real firewall enforcement, Q-learning/V2 effectiveness (0 external sessions), session-ML accuracy (no independent labels, no model), cross-network generalisation (E3 macro F1 0.115), Windows persona against real attackers

The audit's read-only wsl.exe call booted the stopped WSL VM (09:29:51 UTC); the distro's boot configuration auto-started Cowrie (twistd PID 345, 09:29:57 UTC, persona centos_7). The audit did not stop it.
findings.remediation: Stop it yourself if it should not be running (e.g. `wsl --shutdown`).

findings.title: The changed-files scan used find with -not -path (not -prune), so it traversed the three protected ai-engine/experiments directories (directory entries and mtimes only; no file opened, read, hashed or printed). Result: only docs/CAPABILITIES.md, docs/DEMO_STARTUP_AND_TROUBLESHOOTING.md and docs/PERSONAS.md were newer than the Rank 7 evidence (Rank 7's own documentation edits).
